title: aibench config
description: Config for aibench (aibench.yaml): profiles say which gateway/provider to talk to, prompt sets say what is being tested — the two switch independently. Mirrors the strict parser in internal/config — unknown keys are errors there and here. The app never writes this file; it persists into settings.json beside it.

prompts.description: Prompt set name → what is being tested: an instructions file plus 0..n starter scripts and 0..n tools references. Profiles pin a set by name (prompt:); a profile without a pin runs with the first set by name.

tools.description: Tools key → tool file path (declarations + bindings; see docs/tool-catalog.md). Prompt sets reference keys, so one file serves many sets.

kind.description: What stands behind the endpoint — always declared, never defaulted. model: model inference, this tool owns prompt + params. agent: a hosted agent owning its instructions/tools server-side (responses wire + server state implied; declaring type/store/prompt.file fails loudly).

prompt.description: Optional pin: the prompt set (a top-level prompts: name) this profile starts on. Without it the session keeps its current set. An agent may pin only a starters-only set — it owns its instructions server-side.

api.description: What to speak and where: the wire shape, the route, and the verbatim headers/query the endpoint needs.

provider.description: Whose protocol to speak (the SDK). Default: openai.

type.description: Which of the provider's APIs — the wire shape. openai: chat (default) or responses; anthropic implies messages (omit the field). Forbidden on kind: agent (responses implied).

store.description: The responses api's stateful mode (the official store parameter): responses stored server-side, requests chained on previous_response_id. Responses api only; forbidden on kind: agent (implied).

stream.description: The official stream parameter: true streams deltas, false makes one buffered request. Kind-aware default (model: true; agent: false — the hosted-agent endpoint returns an empty event stream). Responses api only.

base.description: The whole route: a base URL template that may carry {model} (Azure deployment routes); the SDK appends the operation path (/chat/completions, /responses, /v1/messages).

model.description: Model name — or the deployment name that fills {model}; also the request body's model and the pricing key. On agent endpoints it must match the agent's own model deployment.

headers.description: Extra request headers sent verbatim (e.g. a gateway's subscription key as api-key). Values expand ${VAR} from the credentials file; redacted in the capture.

query.description: Extra query parameters sent verbatim (e.g. api-version). Same ${VAR} expansion; values show unredacted in the capture — no secrets here.

auth.description: The credentials source. Credentials never live in the yaml.

credentials.description: Env-format file holding only the secrets this profile's auth method needs (a relative path resolves against the directory you run aibench from), or "env" for the process environment.

promptset.description: One prompt set: what is being tested against whatever endpoint is active.

instructions.description: The system-prompt file (markdown + YAML frontmatter params, hot-reloaded) — the responses api's term; on chat/messages it lands as the system message. Omit for a starters-only set.

starters.description: Starter-script files, each one scripted conversation (markdown, one ## title per prompt). Declaring any makes launch offer the /starters selection — nothing auto-sends; also played headless by `aibench send --script`.

tools.description: Keys of the top-level tools map, merged in list order (tools arrays concatenate; any other colliding field or binding name is an error).
